title: exp601_tier_quota_test: tenant tier-profile override not applied — resolver returns platform default (200000) instead of configured override (10) — 4 blocks
affected_areas: src/exp (effects/quota tier-profile resolution area — exact file not yet identified)
symptom: TC-EXP-601-01 ('quota policy resolves the effective profile from the active config surface') asserts the resolved profile's max_entity_records_total is 10 (a deliberately small test override) but gets 200000 (the evident platform default) instead. TC-EXP-601-02, 03, 04 (quota middleware rejection tests for entity/file/sandbox-allocation writes) fail downstream of the same misresolved profile.
root_cause_analysis: Not yet traced to the specific resolver function or table. TC-EXP-601-01 is the root: whatever config-surface lookup is supposed to find and apply a tenant-specific tier-profile override is not finding it, so the resolver falls through to (or never leaves) the platform default of 200000. Needs a read of the quota/tier-profile resolution code to determine whether this is a lookup-key mismatch (e.g. wrong tenant_id used for the lookup), a missing seed row in the test fixture, or a config-precedence bug (default evaluated/cached before the override is applied). Not observed in any prior ISS file — appears to be a genuinely new, distinct defect, not a symptom of the other ISS-0184 clusters (no SQL error in the postgres server log correlates with this test's timestamp window; it's a pure application-logic mismatch, not a query failure).
impact: 4 of the ~93 real failures in ISS-0184/GH-517's diagnosed set. Blocks the Green-Main Gate the same as every other ISS-0184 cluster. Also a genuine product-correctness concern: if tier-quota overrides silently don't apply, tenants could exceed their contracted limits in production.
acceptance_criteria: The tier-profile override resolution path is traced from config source to the resolver's return value
Root cause identified as lookup-key mismatch, missing seed data, or precedence bug
TC-EXP-601-01 through 04 pass against a freshly migrated database
related: ISS-0184 / GH #517 - the holding issue this was split from
notes: Filed per CLAUDE.md 'No Issue Left Local-Only' and ISS-0184's acceptance criteria explicit split allowance. Diagnosis-only pass; root cause not fully pinned, flagged as needing a code-level read beyond this pass's scope.

confirmed_root_cause.summary: repository_artifacts is a GLOBAL_REGISTRY table (canonical home: public) whose stray tenant_default shadow copy was left un-dropped by migration GBL-134. The test's fixture INSERTs run through TestHarness.conn (search_path = 'tenant_default,public', see tests/integration/helpers.zig:256 configureTestSearchPath), so the unqualified INSERT INTO repository_artifacts in insertQuotaPolicyArtifact (tests/integration/exp601_tier_quota_test.zig:51-65) resolves to tenant_default.repository_artifacts (confirmed present as a real distinct relation via `\dt tenant_default.repository_artifacts`). The activation row inserted by ensureQuotaPolicyActivation (exp601_tier_quota_test.zig:67-76) correctly lands in public.tenant_artifact_activations, because GBL-134 (migrations/GBL-134_iss0185_drop_global_registry_shadows.sql:69) DID drop that table's tenant_default shadow. The resolver (src/config/loader.zig loadConfigArtifact, lines 204-215) runs on a POOL connection whose search_path is 'public' only (LEGACY_RLS storage_mode is pool.zig's default for test tenants per applyRequestStorageRouting, src/db/pool.zig:277-282, since TestHarness.provisionTenant at tests/integration/helpers.zig:1116-1124 never sets tenant.storage_mode). Its query `SELECT ra.content_json::text FROM tenant_artifact_activations taa JOIN repository_artifacts ra ON ra.version_id = taa.active_version_id WHERE taa.tenant_id = $1 ...` (loader.zig:206-212) therefore finds the activation row in public.tenant_artifact_activations but the JOIN against public.repository_artifacts returns 0 rows, because the actual artifact content_json the test inserted is sitting in tenant_default.repository_artifacts instead. loadActiveQuotaPolicy returns ConfigError.ConfigNotFound (mapped to null at loader.zig:218), so quota_policy.loadEffectiveQuotaProfile (src/config/quota_policy.zig:100-113) never calls applyPolicyJson and falls through to defaultProfileForTier(.standard) = max_entity_records_total 200000 (quota_policy.zig:325-335) instead of the test's override of 10.
confirmed_root_cause.upstream_defect: migrations/GBL-134_iss0185_drop_global_registry_shadows.sql's v_tables allow-list (lines 45-70) contains only 24 of the 37 tables that docs/issue-reports/ISS-0185-diagnosis.yaml itself classifies as GLOBAL_REGISTRY (global_registry_tenant_default_is_stray, lines 54-87 of that file). 13 are missing from the drop array, including repository_artifacts (diagnosis line 80) plus api_token_audit, artifact_versions, event_payload_store, event_type_registry_producers, instance_definition_snapshots, instance_waits, oidc_migration_item, oidc_migration_job, registry_idp_operation_ledger, tenant, tenant_hostnames, variable_schemas. Verified by diffing the diagnosis's classification_table.global_registry_tenant_default_is_stray list against GBL-134's v_tables array. GBL-134's own header comment claims full coverage of the 37-item GLOBAL classification but the implementation only covers 24 -- this is the true upstream defect; ISS-0617's test failures are a downstream symptom of it for the one table exp601 happens to touch (repository_artifacts).
confirmed_root_cause.verification_method: Live-ran `zig build test-integration-exp601-diag` (temporary build.zig step, reverted after use) against workspace r-co-2's test DB (BPM_TEST_DB_URL=postgres://bpm:bpm@localhost:5453/bpm_test). Added temporary std.debug.print tracing in src/config/loader.zig (search_path, row counts in public vs unqualified) and in the test file itself (same-connection row counts in tenant_default.repository_artifacts vs public.repository_artifacts vs public.tenant_artifact_activations, using harness.conn directly so results are visible within the same uncommitted transaction that performed the inserts). Observed: search_path=public on the pool connection; public.tenant_artifact_activations count=0 from the pool's perspective (activation row not yet visible cross-transaction at that trace point, later confirmed present); and decisively, from harness.conn in the SAME transaction: tenant_default.repository_artifacts has row for the inserted version_id (count=1), public.repository_artifacts has 0 rows for that version_id, public.tenant_artifact_activations correctly has 1 row for the tenant. Independently confirmed via `docker exec r-co-2-db_test-1 psql -U bpm -d bpm_test -c "\dt tenant_default.repository_artifacts"` that this table exists as a real, distinct relation in tenant_default (not just a search_path artifact), while `\dt tenant_default.tenant_artifact_activations` returns 'Did not find any relation' (correctly dropped by GBL-134). All temporary debug code and the temporary build.zig step were reverted before completing this handoff; `git diff --stat` on build.zig, src/config/loader.zig, and tests/integration/exp601_tier_quota_test.zig is empty, and `zig build` was re-run clean after reverting.
confirmed_root_cause.test_blocks_relationship: All 4 test blocks (TC-EXP-601-01 through 04) share this single root cause via a common failure chain, not 4 independent bugs. TC-EXP-601-01 is the direct hit: it calls quota_policy.loadEffectiveQuotaProfile directly and asserts max_entity_records_total == 10, observing 200000 instead (exp601_tier_quota_test.zig:117) -- this is the root-cause assertion. TC-EXP-601-02, 03, 04 all call quota_middleware.check (src/api/middleware/quota_enforcement.zig), which internally calls the same loadEffectiveQuotaProfile as its first step -- so they inherit the same misresolved (200000/etc.) profile rather than the zeroQuotaPolicyJson() override those tests configure, and their 429-rejection assertions fail downstream because the (wrong) resolved limits never get exceeded by the tests' requested deltas. Distinct, NOT part of this root cause: TC-EXP-601-04's second failure mode (PgError.ServerError on `INSERT INTO instance_waits ...`, exp601_tier_quota_test.zig:265) is a separate, likely schema-related issue on the instance_waits table -- instance_waits is itself one of the 13 GLOBAL_REGISTRY tables missing from GBL-134's drop array (see upstream_defect list above), so it may share the identical upstream mechanism, but this was not traced to file:line precision in this pass and should be confirmed separately if it persists once the GBL-134 gap is fixed.
